title: Mortal Kombat X
text: If you like fighting games, GET OVER HERE! Loved this back in the day.  Used to play on my uncle's Megadrive.  Now it's bigger, better and more beautiful than ever. Lots of characters with a huge selection of moves.  Easy to pick up and difficult to master. I like the Mortal Kombat series for the gore and violence (which might not be to everyone's taste). Aside from the fighting, there's LOADS to do here.  Story, towers, online, casual fighting and I even enjoyed the Krypt levels where you buy and unlock extra things.  There's also a mode with lots of modifiers which randomize the fights. The story is like a Saturday morning kids show - nothing special.  Lots of teenagers with daddy issues and lots of well used tropes but hey - it's a fighting game, waddaya expect? Anyway, this game is gorgeous, plays fast and is really satisfying.  I never played online so can't judge that side of it but really like this game a lot.

title: Mortal Kombat X
text: MORTAL KOMBAT X: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ I purchased this game simply due to the amazing graphics I saw on the trailer. To be honest with you, I am not a real fan of this type of game. I do own a couple of titles (including Mortal Kombat 9) but rarely play them. What impressed me on my first attempt was how easy the controls (moves) were to master which to me was a massive plus. From this, I jumped into the story mode and was just blown away by this game, from the cinematic scenes to the game play! At first, you will have to choose one of five factions to join (you will have challenges to achieve on a daily basis to help your faction ranking). After choosing one faction, you will be directed to the game menu where you will be able to select a mode of play.  You will have several options: one player, two players and online mode. Each fight you win, you will get coins (this will vary upon successful combos) which you will be able to use in the Krypt section to unlock plenty of gizmos by opening tombs. My suggestion to you is to amalgamate as many coins as possible because the krypt is fairly big and has many tombs to ravage. Mortal Kombat X has absolutely splendid graphics, runs smoothly and the controls are easy to master. Positives: ~~~~~~~~ -	Splendid cinematic scenes (story mode) -	Great control system -	Very addictive -	 Plenty of achievements -	Trading cards Negatives: ~~~~~~~~ -	Big download but well worth it Fun, addictive, visually grandiose, just a cracker of a fighting game! 10/10

title: Mount & Blade: With Fire & Sword
text: This game is based on the 1998 Polish movie "Fire and Sword".  It provides a historical backdrop for 1650's warfare in central Europe, including Cossack, Tatar, Muscovite, Polish and Swedish units and cities.  Some mods extend the map and available units too. Game is ungoddly awesome.  Something about riding a horse while shooting - it's a similar feeling to flying.  You can command units with great precision and it takes a while to master.  But what a rush to play - even though I completely suck at fighting, buidling up an army and working out the tactics is great.  The AI is is pretty good too (I'm guessing completely based on Behavior Trees).  Sometimes I play the sniper while the rest of the army is skirmishing - really hard to get in a good shot - and very satisfying when it connects.  These are ancient guns and not rifled, so they aren't very accurate from long-range. Also playing solo (no army yet) and taking out the horse of some jerk who's tearing me up - it's a big rush of adrenhaline! Economy is quite clever, where you can drive down market prices and then send caravans at a discount.  Can also take out loans in a pinch. If you quit the tutorial immediately, then it's a little more challenging to start with no money, no gun and no horse - I think this is the best way to play it.

title: Mushroom 11
text: While it probably won't be for everyone, Mushroom 11 is one of the most interesting/original puzzle platformers that I have played in a while. In Mushroom 11 you play as a creature that can almost instantly re-grow its' cells. This means that damaged or "erased" cells will re-grow to the creature. The main mechanic in the game involves erasing part of the creature which makes that part of the creature re-grow somewhere else which you use to move the creature and solve the game's puzzles. The game does a great job using this mechanic to create some interesting puzzles and boss fights. For the most part the mechanic works really well but the game does occasionally run into situations where the game keeps adding the new cells to an area of the creature where you didn't  want them to be moved to. This means that you sometimes have to waste time erasing the same part of the creature. While I haven't finished the game yet I am through four of the seven levels and I have played the game for a little over three hours. I am guessing that the game is around six hours long. If you think the game's concept sounds interesting I think you will enjoy Mushroom 11. If you are a little more unsure about the game, I think you should at least consider purchasing the game during a sale since it is a really unique experience that I think most people should enjoy. Note: I received a free review copy of the game from the developer.

title: Mushroom 11
text: I finished this game yesterday and it was a very nice and unique puzzle game. The main game feature is something I had never seen before. Your character is what I assume is Mushroom 11. A kind of goo with the ability to always regenerate itself to it's full mass. And the only input you have is some kind of eraser. You have to "erase" some part of the mushroom to make it regenerate on the other side. You do this through 7 levels of increasing difficulty, each with tons of new features. The levels take 20 to 40 minutes each to complete on the first run. The game never gets old because you rarely have to do the same thing twice. You ride a cart and do sick jumps, you ride rockets, you race boulders and buildings falling down and you sculpt yourself into a bridge. There is also 7 bosses at the end of each level and each feel like a unique and fun challenge. The worse that can happen is to get frustrated because of how hard the puzzle can be. Seriously, f*ck level 7. It took me 2 hours 20 to beat and the last boss wasn't even fun. I wish it would have been 2 shorter levels instead. Anyway, maybe that's just me being bad. I just want to do a heads up : This game can get frustrating. There is one last thing I'd like to adress. Have you seen the video by gbay99? As a summary, he talks about his experience with lore in video games, specifically Runescape where the lore is not forced on the players but there to explore and discover. And Mushroom 11 feels exactly this way to me. Earlier, I wrote "Your character is what I assume is Mushroom 11." That's because I was never told that. There is no cutscenes, no cinematics, no hidden diary. You just start there and walk through levels. Just the first level gives you the setting of the story and I feel like there are a lot of details about what hapenned in the last two levels. Each boss feel like a weird concrete representation of those hints. Some kind of incarnation of what happenned there. The ending also leave you with more questions than answers. I think this is amazing and very well done! Unique and challenging puzzle game with amazing environnements and setting. Require both agility and wits, but you'll have a rough time if you don't like challenges.

title: Mushroom 11
text: A unique game experience but infuriatingly tough. I should have realized that when gravity is the dominant challenging factor that it was going to hurt. Once the organism starts rolling, there's precious little to be done about it; Even while regenerating it doesn't lose any momentum. I'm not sure about the physics of that. I just wish that the puzzles could exist more like a lab experiment, something you can think about and less of tests of agility and timing. Time is spent carefully paring the organism to make it reach a ledge. But I kept forgetting to let go of the button and I'd accidentally bisect the thing and lose my work. I think that the game design has a fundamental flaw: As you kill cells the organism regrows in random directions, away from your cursor. And there are spills of separated cells that you need to clean-up or else they could become something greater. Because it is random, you can't control what you're getting. So it becomes a cycle of kill, groom, klll, groom, kill, groom, etc. And your effectiveness at being able to do this and keep the thing reasonably under control will determine whether you succeed or fail.

title: Mushroom 11
text: A great little game. Mushroom 11 is a great platformer for people of any age, it does not require cat like reflexes or super difficult button sequencing, nor any quicktime events. You might think it's must not be much of a platformer without haing to mash the jump button but the game works great using its unique mechanic of morping you green goop with just the mouse. For me the game was very easy, with most if the obsticles taking one or two tries to complete. It balances difficulty with checkpoints between difficult obsticle and allows for you to contine the boss fights even when you die. I found this game to be enjoyable and great for relaxing after work or some mindless fun on a lazy sunday afternoon. For those who find the game too easy there are acheivments that will make the levels much more difficult to complete and might be quite stressful. With beautiful graphics and flawless gameplay as well as the G rated content (no naughty stuff) I would this game for kids and adults alike.

title: Mushroom 11
text: I feel bad, but I am giving this game a mild "Not recommended" rating.  I feel bad because it is such an original concept and really is a good puzzle game... but it is so hard and very, very frustrating especially on the last 2-3 chapters. In the game, you control an amobea / blob like creature.  You move by erasing part of yourself, which causes the remaining leftovers to grow in a somewhat random fashion.  Your creature can take on almost any shape, but getting how you want is not always so easy.  The goal of the game is to just reach the end of each chapter, of which there are 7.  Each level also ends with a boss, he being just another puzzle but where you need to somehow destroy him.  Things start out simple with you just needing to reach up to grab things and cross empty spaces.  By the end you will be pushing buttons, riding rockets, pushing balls and racing to make a bridge for them and many other complicated things. This is all great but the levels are simply too long and many of the puzzles are too fiddly.  Since you grow in a somewhat random fashion, you can know what you want to do and still fail miserably at making your creature do it.  A few of the puzzles in particular will take the average player 10 to 20 attempts to complete them (you riding a rocket across a pool of acid for example).  If these difficult puzzles would have been reduced and the chapters been reduced in length, the game would have been fun and I would have recommended this.  Most players simply won't have the patience to get through to the end of the game, I almost gave up on it myself.  Those with lots of patience might want to try it out though if the concept looks intriguing, others should pass.

title: Mushroom 11
text: A unique game experience but infuriatingly tough. I should have realized that when gravity is the dominant challenging factor that it was going to hurt. Once the organism starts rolling, there's precious little to be done about it; Even while regenerating it doesn't lose any momentum. I'm not sure about the physics of that. I just wish that the puzzles could exist more like a lab experiment, something you can think about and less of tests of agility and timing. Time is spent carefully paring the organism to make it reach a ledge. But I kept forgetting to let go of the button and I'd accidentally bisect the thing and lose my work. I think that the game design has a fundamental flaw: As you kill cells the organism regrows in random directions, away from your cursor. And there are spills of separated cells that you need to clean-up or else they could become something greater. Because it is random, you can't control what you're getting. So it becomes a cycle of kill, groom, klll, groom, kill, groom, etc. And your effectiveness at being able to do this and keep the thing reasonably under control will determine whether you succeed or fail.

title: Mushroom 11
text: Unique physics gameplay, beautiful hand-drawn like graphics. Can be slightly frustrating at times, but nothing major. Recommended. EDIT: I managed to get to the final boss, but could not beat it. Way too difficult for my patience. Now that I've seen most of the content I also think that the game is a bit overrated. It's good, but not that great. My biggest complaint is the "puzzle" aspect of the game. In general I like when puzzles in games take a bit effort to figure out, and once you do get it, they offer reasonable challenge to solve them. There are few worst case scenarios: a) puzzles that are very easy to figure out and incredibly tedious to solve, b) puzzles that are tedious to figure out and also tedious to solve and c) puzzles that you manage to solve without figuring them out (by luck, by persistence etc). Unfortunately a lot of the puzzles in this game fall in the category A, and some in B. Many times I figured out the "puzzle" immediately but solving it was so frustrating and lot of retries were needed. The controls are bit arbitrary and bit frustrating by design as you can only cull the mushroom and not say where it should grow. But this is ok, it's the thing in the game. The game also has quite good camera work in principle, but unfortunately together with the controls this creates a huge source of frustration. Even if you keep your mouse still, the moving camera affects the area where the mouse is culling the mushroom, and there's also a feedback loop where changing mushroom shape affects the movement of the camera. This was not bad as it propably sounds, but at times it was infuriating. Sometimes I was wanting for the mouse to move in WORLDSPACE, not in screenspace. That might have solved some of the issues... Anyway, I do recommend this game. It's one of its kind, and really interesting take on the physics puzzle platformers. Despite all the frustration.
